title: NRCS runoff forecast tail errors aligned across five drainage regions at 221 sites in 2006-2025
abstract: We tested whether low-runoff errors in NRCS April 1 forecasts of April-July adjusted volume aligned across drainage regions. We reused a published archive and fixed a complete 2006-2025 panel of 221 sites in five HUC2 regions. Each region received equal weight. The variance of the annual mean low-tail failure share was 2.26 times the exact reference under independent regional timing, with a 95% whole-year bootstrap interval of 1.07-3.01. Independent permutations moved each region as a whole and kept its internal dependence and error rates; the one-sided Monte Carlo p-value was 0.00010. Circular shifts and within-decade permutations also supported alignment. After each site was assigned exactly two low-tail years from its twenty ranked normalized forecast errors, the variance ratio remained 2.07 (1.14-2.84). Unequal local tail rates cannot alone explain this result. High errors also aligned. Only one year had at least three regions with 25% of sites below the published lower limit, so joint return periods remain unresolved. This is an archive dependence diagnostic, not a forward forecast or a false joint probability issued by NRCS. Twenty years, a selected complete panel, adjusted flows and archive revisions limit inference. The physical source is unresolved. Code, source hashes, regional aggregates and a retrieval recipe are included; raw and site-level data stay external.

display.caption: Low-tail errors align across five drainage regions. The lower panels set every site tail frequency to exactly 10%. Independent regional timing preserves all within-region dependence.

citations.reason: Reuses source snapshots and MIT loading code; extends the marginal audit to cross-region dependence with fixed local tail frequencies.
Established dependence-template method; no claim of a new dependence theorem.
